title: Guzheng (Chinese zither)
summary: The guzheng is a long Chinese board zither whose twenty-one silk or steel strings each rest on a small movable bridge. The right hand plucks and sweeps the strings while the left presses them behind the bridges to bend and shade each note.
howToPlay: Eleven strings and a sweep bar are drawn across the board, low notes on the left and high notes on the right.
A bead glides along a string toward the bridge. Pluck that string just as the bead arrives.
When the wide sweep bar lights, draw a finger across the strings for a rippling run.
Begin with the rising and falling water phrase, then try the quick running tune and the answering phrases.
rules: The strings are tuned to a five-note scale: D, E, F sharp, A and B, repeated in each higher octave.
A pluck on the beat scores perfect, a near pluck scores good, and stray plucks cost points.
The sweep lane sounds every string from low to high in one run.
Each tune is played through twice.
Watch and learn plays a tune for you so you can hear the phrase first.
heritageNote: Zithers of this kind have been played in China for well over two thousand years, and the modern instrument carries twenty-one or more strings. Players are admired for rippling runs, rolling tremolo and for bending notes by pressing a string beyond its bridge.
